title: Map to battle handoff
kicker: World and empire · commit a legion into a fight
hook: **WIP:** commit a legion into a fight — the map hands a battle a request and consumes an outcome. Not finished / not fully playable yet.

blindSpots.meaning: Not finished. Full fantasy needs interactive battles you play yourself.
Map → battle request → outcome back to the map. Not a separate save and not a lawn launch by itself.
Sending a legion into the test — travel into a fight, not only standing on a node.
A fight you play (initiative, action bar, targets) — WIP as a stage; expeditions stay auto-resolve.

alsoTrue: Lane-board presentation hangs on the [three-layer world](three-layer-world) Vision.
You can still march, claim, and End Turn without this handoff.

sections.title: What it will feel like
paras: You commit a legion into a fight from the graph.
The map hands the battle a request; when the fight ends, the map consumes the outcome and the war continues.
diagram: legion on map  ->  commit  ->  battle request

sections.title: What you do today
paras: Advance the shipped map without expecting a finished playable battle stage from every contact.
Treat missing commit-to-battle prompts as unfinished work.

sections.title: What it depends on
paras: Interactive battles you play yourself are WIP — same combat language, your hands on the action bar.
Until that stage hardens, the handoff cannot feel finished.
sections.note: See [interactive battles](interactive-battles) when that teach page exists; combat pillar covers the language.

doTitle: What you do while it is WIP
doSteps: Keep using march, claim, and End Turn on the world map.
When a commit-to-battle control appears, follow it and read the outcome back on the map.
Do not confuse this with launching a casual lawn match from Sanctum.
doNote: Stop when handoff ≠ lawn shortcut. Related: [world map](world-map), [three-layer world](three-layer-world).

mixUps.q: Why doesn’t contact always open a battle I play?
mixUps.a: Map→battle handoff and interactive battles are WIP.
No. It is a battle stage fed by the map — lawn remains its own first core loop.

mixUps.q: Does the map ignore the fight result?
mixUps.a: Design consumes the outcome back into the war — that loop is what “handoff” means.
